If factoring doesn't work, use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / 2a. Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac) first - if it's negative, you get complex solutions. Don't panic if it seems messy; take it step by step. I always double-check my arithmetic.

Stationary points are where the function's slope is zero. First, find the derivative f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x - these are your stationary points' x-coordinates.
